definitions.gloss: to creep up; to steal near; to sneak up on
definitions.explanation: To approach quietly and stealthily, so as not to be noticed. Used both literally (a person sneaking up) and figuratively (danger, old age, or fear approaching gradually).

examples.english: The cat creeps up on its prey.

examples.japanese: ⟦{背後|はいご}→背後：18212_haigo⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る⟦{足音|あしおと}→足音：02991_ashioto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえた→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: I heard footsteps sneaking up from behind.

examples.japanese: ⟦{不安|ふあん}→不安：00836_fuan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}ってくる⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: I felt anxiety quietly creeping up on me.

notes:
USAGE:
Literally used for people or animals sneaking up on someone. Figuratively, it is commonly used with abstract subjects like ⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧ (danger), ⟦{老|お}い→老い：01842_oi⟧ (old age), ⟦{不安|ふあん}→不安：00836_fuan⟧ (anxiety), or ⟦{影|かげ}→影：02191_kage⟧ (shadow) to describe something approaching ominously and gradually.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{背後|はいご}→背後：18212_haigo⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る (to sneak up from behind)
- ⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る (danger creeps up)
- ⟦{老|お}い→老い：01842_oi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る (old age creeps up)
- ⟦そっと→そっと：03321_sotto⟧{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る (to creep up quietly)

Godan verb (る→ら{行|ぎょう}): {忍|しの}び{寄|よ}らない, {忍|しの}び{寄|よ}ります, {忍|しの}び{寄|よ}って
